### pipeWithValve3d

This example shows how to use STL files for the channel geometry and for an obstacle in it. It describes the flow in a pipe with a valve under a predefined angle. The pipe geometry is included via `STLreader<T> pipe( "pipe.stl", converter.getPhysDeltaX(), 0.001)` and the valve geometry via `STLreader<T> valve( "valve.stl", converter.getPhysDeltaX(), 0.001)`. Both geometries were created in FreeCAD and exported in STL format with mm units. The case is discretized with a D3Q19 lattice and `BGKdynamics`. On the inlet and outlet planes of the pipe, the `boundary::set<boundary::InterpolatedVelocity>(sLattice, superGeometry, 3)` and `boundary::set<boundary::InterpolatedPressure>(sLattice, superGeometry, 4)` boundaries are set. On the walls of the pipe and of the valve `BounceBack` dynamics are used as no-slip boundary conditions. For the definition of inlet and outlet material numbers, the maximal and minimal coordinates of the pipe STL surrounding cells are used:

```{.cpp}
superGeometry.rename( 0,2,indicator );
superGeometry.rename( 2,1,pipe );
superGeometry.clean();

Vector<T,3> origin = superGeometry.getStatistics().getMinPhysR(2);
origin[1] += converter.getPhysDeltaX()/2.;
origin[2] += converter.getPhysDeltaX()/2.;

Vector<T,3> extend = superGeometry.getStatistics().getMaxPhysR(2);
extend[1] = extend[1]-origin[1]-converter.getPhysDeltaX()/2.;
extend[2] = extend[2]-origin[2]-converter.getPhysDeltaX()/2.;

// Set material number for inflow
origin[0] = superGeometry.getStatistics().getMinPhysR(2)[0]
    -converter.getPhysDeltaX();
extend[0] = 2*converter.getPhysDeltaX();
IndicatorCuboid3D<T> inflow( extend,origin );
superGeometry.rename( 2,3,inflow );
```

The valve inside the pipe is rotated using the rotation indicator `IndicatorRotate<T,3> valveRot(rotationPoint, rotationAxis, rotationAngle, valve)`.

To get a stable simulation, a velocity ramp is used at the beginning of the simulation:

```{.cpp}
PolynomialStartScale<T,int> StartScale( iTmaxStart, T( 1 ) );
// Creates and sets the Poiseuille inflow profile using functors
int iTvec[1] = {iT};
T frac[1] = {};
StartScale( frac,iTvec );
std::vector<T> maxVelocity(3,0);
maxVelocity[0] = 2.25*frac[0]*converter.getCharLatticeVelocity();
T distance2Wall = converter.getPhysDeltaX()/2.;
CirclePoiseuille3D<T> poiseuilleU(superGeometry, 3, 
    maxVelocity[0], distance2Wall);
sLattice.defineU( superGeometry, 3, poiseuilleU );
```

The simulation results in a flow around the valve with the velocity field visualized in the following @fig-pipeWithValve.
